appraisal_events.evidence: ce n'est pas le plus spirituel, le plus instruit, le mieux relationné des hommes... qui devient un Bergotte (les contemporains le tinssent-ils pour moins homme d'esprit que Swann et moins savant que Brichot)
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator retrospectively concludes that becoming a genius like Bergotte depends not on wit or erudition — in which contemporaries ranked him below Swann and Brichot — but on a rarer mirror-like capacity, elevating his achievement over conventional markers of brilliance.

appraisal_events.evidence: il est probable que Swann, si fin, si purgé de tout ridicule haïssable, eût été incapable d'écrire la Cousine Bette et le Curé de Tours
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator credits Swann's exquisite refinement and freedom from vulgarity, but concludes this same fineness would have made him incapable of the raw genius that produced Balzac's masterpieces, a backhanded diminishment paired with praise.

appraisal_events.evidence: duc de Guermantes ne m'avait certes pas donné l'impression de cet adorable modèle des grâces juvéniles... Mais il faut songer que duc de Guermantes avait alors sept ans, que l'écrivain était sa tante, et que même les maris qui doivent divorcer... vous font un grand éloge de leur femme
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's own impression of the duke did not match the idealized 'adorable model of juvenile graces' painted by a memoir, though the passage immediately undercuts this by noting the source's biased affection, leaving the assessment unsettled.

status_effects.explanation: Bergotte's genius is affirmed as resting on a rare inner capacity rather than surface wit or learning, raising his standing relative to more conventionally brilliant figures.
Despite praised refinement, Swann is marked as incapable of the kind of raw genius that produced great literature, a mild diminishment relative to genius.

The idealized childhood portrait of the duke is deflated by the narrator's unimpressed direct experience, though the passage's own explanation of memoir bias tempers the certainty of this diminishment.

ambiguities: The duc de Guermantes passage both records a deflating impression and explains it away as the product of a biased, affectionate memoir source, so it is unclear whether the passage intends a genuine diminishment of the duke or merely a comment on the unreliability of Mémoires in general.

The Swann/Balzac comparison mixes praise of Swann's refinement with an implied incapacity for raw genius; the net local direction is read as mildly diminishing but the passage does not force a single verdict.
